searchText: Hello! Currently working on bringing Prysm up to date with v0.8.2, although after taking a look at each of the `slots.yaml` in <https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-spec-tests/tree/v0.8.2/tests/mainnet/phase0/sanity/slots/pyspec_tests> it seems something is off. Each of the `slots.yaml` in those folders look like: ``` 128 ... ``` as you can see in https://media.githubusercontent.com/media/ethereum/eth2.0-spec-tests/v0.8.2/tests/mainnet/phase0/sanity/slots/pyspec_tests/double_empty_epoch/slots.yaml Is this intentional? **protolambda** It's perfectly valid yaml, just a single integer. In Go it's just a matter of passing the address of an allocated int to the yaml decoder. Don't overcomplicate the simple stuff is the idea. But if it's a real pain for some reason, we may decide to change it No worries, was just offset by the `...` after the integer. Retrieving it won't be a problem. https://yaml.org/spec/1.0/#ns-ns-document-end Ahhh, I see! Thank you Yeah, somethings off with bls 0.8.3 spec tests pubkeys has 96 bytes and signatures 192 bytes Those are most likely uncompressed pubkeys and signatures I thought so as well, but I get wierd results if I set first part as X and second part as Y I get infinity or something **benjaminion** (in reply to **<@545555441518772225>**) I've just had a quick look through the 0.8.3 BLS tests, and they seem ok to me: 48 bytes (96 hex chars) for pubkeys; 96 bytes (192 hex chars) for signatures. Can you point to a specific test with this issue? sec i need to switch terminal. I might have made error converting to buffer. **shahankhatch** Could someone please point me to some existing BLS benchmark code? I'd like to check my understanding of the expected benchmark. **shahankhatch** Would the following be it? https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/blob/83083b9c659e2b2087409fbd8fac8a545cf2d1d9/shared/bls/bls_benchmark_test.go **shahankhatch** Any other links would be appreciated. I will give you some links Phore BLS, what prysm is using, benches, `go test -bench` : https://github.com/phoreproject/bls/blob/master/g1pubs/verify_benchmark_test.go Milagro BLS, sigma prime fork, what most teams are using in some form or another. Run with `cargo bench --features="bench"` https://github.com/sigp/milagro_bls/blob/master/benches/bls381_benches.rs **shahankhatch** Thanks @protolambda! What is the correct `parentRoot` for a block next to Genesis? `genesis_state.finalized_checkpoint.root` is a zero hash while `signing_root(genesis_state.latest_block_header)` returns a real hash root. This discrepancy leads to several tweaks around processing genesis block and it's direct descendant. the block on top of the genesis block should have `parent_root` that is `signing_root(genesis_state.latest_block_header)`, right? the state transition should then work correctly there is some "delay" around having valid justification/finality data in the state for the first few epochs but it avoids having more special casing in the phase 0 spec that we will all have to maintain in perpetuity

as you can see in https://media.githubusercontent.com/media/ethereum/eth2.0-spec-tests/v0.8.2/tests/mainnet/phase0/sanity/slots/pyspec_tests/double_empty_epoch/slots.yaml

excerpts.author: eth2_bridge_bot
excerpts.content:
**protolambda**
It's perfectly valid yaml, just a single integer. In Go it's just a matter of passing the address of an allocated int to the yaml decoder. Don't overcomplicate the simple stuff is the idea. But if it's a real pain for some reason, we may decide to change it

What is the correct `parentRoot` for a block next to Genesis? 
`genesis_state.finalized_checkpoint.root` is a zero hash while `signing_root(genesis_state.latest_block_header)` returns a real hash root. This discrepancy leads to several tweaks around processing genesis block and it's direct descendant.
